text: I'll start with the pod and the cluster capacity.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks for a CPU request of "512" in its pod template. In Kubernetes that value is 512 whole cores, not 512 millicores; the "m" suffix is missing. The only node in the cluster, node/incident-lab-control-plane, has 6 allocatable CPUs, so no node can satisfy the request and the scheduler rejects the pod with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu". Pod fraud/fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh therefore stays in phase Pending with PodScheduled=False and never runs, so the Deployment reports ready=0/1 and no fraud scores are produced. Changing the request to "512m" makes it schedulable.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512", i.e. 512 whole cores, where "512m" (0.512 core) was intended; node/incident-lab-control-plane offers only cpu=6/6 allocatable, so the scheduler cannot place the pod and repeatedly emits FailedScheduling "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.", leaving pod fraud/fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh Pending with PodScheduled False and the Deployment at ready=0/1.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is Pending and unscheduled.
The pod is Pending with no node assigned.
The scheduler rejects the pod for insufficient CPU.
evidence.quote: Warning  FailedScheduling  1s    default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.

evidence.claim: The pod's admitted CPU request is 512 cores and PodScheduled is False.
The Deployment pod template requests cpu "512" (whole cores) rather than "512m".
The only node has 6 allocatable CPUs, far less than the request.

ruled_out.alternative: The node is unhealthy or tainted so nothing can schedule there
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The node reports Ready=True and no taints are listed, and the pod has no node selector; the scheduler's only complaint is CPU.

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota or LimitRange in the namespace blocks or inflates the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace contains only a ConfigMap and a ServiceAccount besides the workload; no quota or limitrange objects exist.

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken (crash loop / pull failure)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never got a node, so no container ever started; its only condition is PodScheduled False.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks for a CPU request of "512" in its pod template. In Kubernetes that value means 512 whole cores, not 512 millicores; the "m" suffix is missing. The only node in the cluster has cpu=6/6 capacity/allocatable, so no node can satisfy the request and the default scheduler rejects the pod with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu". The pod fraud/fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh therefore stays in phase Pending with PodScheduled False and never runs, so the Deployment reports ready=0/1 and the risk team receives no fraud scores. Setting the request to "512m" makes the pod schedulable.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512" — 512 whole cores — where "512m" (0.512 core) was intended, which exceeds the cpu=6/6 capacity/allocatable of every node in the cluster. The default scheduler therefore cannot place the replica and keeps emitting FailedScheduling "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.", so the Deployment stays at ready=0/1 with its replica stuck in phase Pending and PodScheduled False.
